o1.biggest_strength: It builds the launch around the real signal: creators and extension authors bring users who stay, and migration is the launch risk that must be gated before the freeze.
o1.biggest_mistake: It slightly blurs the channel-ranking logic by saying it ranks by stay share while also showing retained-user counts that would put X and Product Hunt above extension authors on raw retained users.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the channel ranking explanation, remove the 'to confirm' items, and only include backup/staged rollout promises if engineering has already committed them.

o2.biggest_strength: It correctly shifts prep effort away from Product Hunt and toward creator walkthroughs, extension authors, migration testing, support readiness and channel tracking.
o2.biggest_mistake: The customer-facing drafts are not finished: they contain placeholders for names, authors, clips, speed numbers and support details, so they are not ready to paste.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace all placeholders with final copy, move creator outreach earlier, and avoid assumptions like engineers being free during code freeze unless already agreed.

reason: Output 1 is the one I could hand to the team and mostly run: it has better dated ownership, stronger launch gates, ready-to-use copy, and a sharper support plan. Output 2 has the right strategy, but the launch-day assets still need filling in before they can go live.
